source_original_center.fact: N=4 high-trial repeated measurement two independent flickering luminance squares; residual difference fluctuations randomized each 13.33ms, initial two-choice decision then stimuli continue for 1.5 seconds allowing redecision. Experiment input is luminance stream, not model latent accumulator.

Psychophysical reverse-correlation of residual framewise evidence conditioned on initial correct/error and final reversal; observer results first-frame strength associated with later change probability and weak latency, while later evidence significantly contributes, participant-wise variable effects.

source_original_center.locator: original Methods extended DDM direct ancestor [3]
source_original_center.fact: Original prior Resulaj et al 2009 postdecision accumulator crosses initial bound then optionally opposite change-of-mind bound; conventional matched difficulty constant across-trial drift predicts no condition-controlled first-frame effect.

source_original_center.locator: main novel original Fig2/3 computational methods
source_original_center.fact: Current extension has source first-frame residual luminance difference contributing EXTERNALLY stimulus-driven across-trial drift offset that DECAYS LINEARLY with time, plus independently additive INTERNAL/endogenous trial drift offset and moment-wise external/internal noise.

Fit model using initial/final behavioral response probabilities and initial/change-of-mind RT quantiles, then PREDICT visual evidence psychophysical kernels not used to fit; simulation 100,000 trials for diagnostic pattern, not independent human data.

source_original_center.locator: main original Fig3 original model variants
source_original_center.fact: Actual augmented externally linked early drift+internal variability reproduces initial-frame psychophysical kernel; same drift variability but stimulus-decoupled predicts WRONG early direction, no across-trial drift predicts NO systematic first-frame effect. Preserve both explicit unfavorable original predictions.

original_empirical_source_reported: Change-of-mind occurred in 23.91% of source trials, 18.53% correcting errors and 5.38% spoiling correct responses
Initial choice correctly predicted on 66.95%, final correctness80.10%, original behavioral observed proportions not recreated from simulation
First-frame interaction with initial accuracy predicts change likelihood chi²(1)42.08 p<8.75e-11, change latency chi²(1)4.27 p=.039
Non-first-frame mean pre-response evidence predicts reversal probability chi²(1)192.36 p<2.20e-16 and speed chi²(1)82.36 p=2.20e-16
Mean evidence 200–400ms more predictive of change likelihood than 0–200ms in current task AIC14961 vs15039 original s006; first frame is NOT sole or best predictor

source_specific_negative_and_limits.locator: main source sample Methods and s002
source_specific_negative_and_limits.fact: Only four heavily sampled participants; rare spoilt-correct and individual heterogeneity weaken cohort generalization.
Identical drift variability decoupled from initial stimulus leads source model wrong-sign first-frame kernel, falsifying source-incompatible variant.
Constant across-trial drift yields no first-frame difference; any apparent tiny fast/slow spoilt-correct difference is rare-trial simulation noise, explicitly source not real effect.
First frame NOT sole or strongest source of later change: later mean evidence especially 200–400ms often stronger predictive empirical signal. Retain contrary stronger late effect.

Trial group where mean entire pre/post sensory evidence favors incorrect response extremely rare around 2.9%; original auxiliary analysis argues source first-frame effect not solely mean-signal confound, small group limits broad inference.
Stimulus onset predictable, low-level visual task favors onset attention; unknown transfer to slower multimodal real-world integration.
Sensory-motor delays and choice button timing differ from latent accumulator boundary crossing; measured movement/response trace cannot be equated with unobserved latent decision state.
Extended DDM model fit from behavior does not prove unique physiological internal snapshot representation or source-only external sensory gain.
